nodes.title: The Econometric Argument
nodes.label: Econometric Argument
nodes.desc: A course in applied econometrics and quantitative reasoning: build a claim, inspect its assumptions, and work out what the evidence permits.

nodes.title: One scatterplot, several possible worlds
nodes.label: Ch. 1: Argument
nodes.desc: Separate the question a dataset can answer from the question a decision requires.

nodes.title: Which population is inside the average?
nodes.label: Ch. 2: Probability
nodes.desc: Use conditioning and expectation to diagnose changes in composition before interpreting an average.

nodes.title: What a fitted line has actually earned
nodes.label: Ch. 3: Projection
nodes.desc: Derive least squares, interpret residualization, and distinguish a projection coefficient from a causal effect.

nodes.title: Precision around the wrong answer
nodes.label: Ch. 4: Uncertainty
nodes.desc: Distinguish sampling uncertainty from bias and choose an uncertainty calculation that matches the design.

nodes.title: Make the comparison before the outcomes arrive
nodes.label: Ch. 5: Design
nodes.desc: Construct a randomized comparison, distinguish its estimand from uptake effects, and inspect the design threats.

nodes.title: The dataset is part of the model
nodes.label: Ch. 6: Measurement
nodes.desc: Trace measurement, missingness, and conditioning decisions into the estimand and its identification.

nodes.title: An instrument moves a choice
nodes.label: Ch. 7: Instruments
nodes.desc: Derive an instrumental-variables target, distinguish validity from strength, and examine what happens when exclusion fails.

nodes.title: A comparison across time needs a counterfactual trend
nodes.label: Ch. 8: Panels
nodes.desc: Derive difference-in-differences, separate fixed effects from identification, and quantify a transparent trend sensitivity.

nodes.title: Find the comparison the institution creates
nodes.label: Ch. 9: Local designs
nodes.desc: Explain what a cutoff or a synthetic comparison identifies, including the conditions that make a convincing picture insufficient.

nodes.title: Let prediction help estimation without choosing the question
nodes.label: Ch. 10: Learning
nodes.desc: Derive an orthogonal partial-linear score and understand the role and limits of sample splitting and nuisance learning.

nodes.title: Tomorrow and elsewhere are different populations
nodes.label: Ch. 11: Dependence
nodes.desc: Connect likelihood, dependent-data forecasting, predictive coverage, and the assumptions needed to transfer an effect.

nodes.title: Make a decision the evidence can support
nodes.label: Ch. 12: Decisions
nodes.desc: Translate effects into a constrained decision, distinguish sensitivity from sampling uncertainty, and assemble an auditable empirical argument.

nodes.title: Trade in the spotlight: enhancing gravity model predictions with nightlights and population-weighted distance measures
nodes.label: Trade in the spotlight (2025)
nodes.desc: A geodesic distance between population-weighted centroids, built from VIIRS nightlights and gridded population, measurably improves gravity-model fit.

meta.question: Does a gravity model fit better when bilateral distance reflects where population and measured economic activity are located within countries?
meta.limit: The preprint does not establish the planned panel, transport-network extension, or structural-gravity validation; those remain development work with no completed results.

nodes.title: Effective distance: a satellite-calibrated bilateral trade-cost panel, 2000-2024
nodes.label: Effective-distance panel
nodes.desc: A planned 2000-2024 panel of bilateral effective distance from nightlights, gridded population, and transport networks; no results yet.

meta.question: Can a time-varying measure of bilateral effective distance represent changes in population, economic activity, infrastructure, and transport corridors?
meta.limit: No completed results, validated panel, coverage claim, or public data release exists yet.

nodes.title: Occlusion and adaptation: a closed-loop spatial-labor model of Ukraine's wartime economic reorganization, 2022-2025
nodes.label: Ukraine occlusion model
nodes.desc: A proposed measurement program for Ukraine's wartime economic activity using administrative, satellite, maritime, and labor data; no results yet.

meta.question: How has Ukraine's wartime economic activity reorganized across space when official measurement is itself disrupted by conflict, occupation, and displacement?
meta.role: Coauthor with Elizaveta Gonchar; contribution statement pending joint ratification
meta.limit: No completed results, index, or ratified contribution statement exists yet.

nodes.title: Redefining Trade Dynamics: Incorporating Network Centrality, Spatial Heterogeneity, and Optimal Transport Theory into Models of International Trade
nodes.label: Dissertation (2024)
nodes.desc: Georgia Tech doctoral dissertation on network centrality in gravity models, population-weighted bilateral distance, and optimal transport in trade.

meta.question: How do network position, within-country spatial heterogeneity, and optimal transport change the representation of international trade?
meta.limit: This record covers the three chapters of the 2024 dissertation. Later papers and datasets that build on them have their own records and statuses.

nodes.title: A unifying framework for economic equilibrium and optimal transport in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces
nodes.label: Equilibrium and optimal transport
nodes.desc: A theoretical working paper connecting economic equilibrium and optimal transport when the economic object is a function or distribution.

meta.question: Under what conditions can economic equilibrium be represented as an optimal-transport problem in an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space?
meta.limit: This record states the paper's question and approach; the theorem statements and their assumptions are in the SSRN manuscript.

nodes.title: The rural mobilization gap in a U.S. place-based tax credit
nodes.label: NMTC rural gap (2026)
nodes.desc: In the New Markets Tax Credit, the raw rural leverage gap of −0.262 falls to −0.047 within the same Community Development Entity; descriptive, noncausal.

meta.question: Does the rural private-leverage gap persist when rural and urban projects are compared within the same Community Development Entity?
meta.role: Sole author; Katia Antunes and Elizaveta Gonchar are acknowledged contributors
meta.limit: The design is descriptive and noncausal, does not identify why intermediaries differ, and leaves the mechanism unresolved.

nodes.title: Penumbra: closed-loop observation under measurement gaps in cross-border trade
nodes.label: Penumbra
nodes.desc: A theory paper in progress on measuring cross-border trade when the act of observing that trade changes what becomes visible.

meta.question: How should a trade model represent settings where the equilibrium changes the observation system used to measure that equilibrium?
meta.limit: The paper is in progress and reports no results yet.

nodes.title: Empirical observation equilibria: the Russian seaborne-crude corridor, 2021-2024
nodes.label: Russian seaborne crude
nodes.desc: A proposed design using AIS tracks, port arrivals, and commodity-flow records to study Russian seaborne crude under sanctions; no results yet.

meta.question: Can public shipping and port records identify the feedback between sanctions-evasion behavior and the observation system used to measure Russian seaborne crude?
meta.limit: No empirical results exist yet; identification, coverage, and data construction remain under development.

nodes.title: AI and the Entry-Level Labor Market
nodes.label: AI and entry-level labor
nodes.desc: An empirical design asking whether early-career employment changed differently in occupations with greater generative-AI exposure; no results yet.

meta.question: Did early-career employment change differently after widespread generative-AI adoption in occupations with greater measured AI exposure?
meta.limit: No empirical results exist yet; the public record describes a design and planned analysis only.
